speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development regarding the POFMA Correction Direction issued on 15 February 2024 that contained details of a couple’s financial situation, including their CPF and MediSave balances, (a) how does this level of disclosure align with the privacy protection standards under the Public Sector (Governance) Act (PSGA); and (b) whether the Ministry considers the detailed personal financial disclosure necessary given that it can lead to identification of the couple concerned.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In particular, Mr Leong falsely claimed the woman’s MediSave account was depleted and that she could, therefore, not afford to continue paying for her hospital physiotherapy sessions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Mr Leong also referred to their low quantum of monthly support they receive, without taking into account that they were eligible to withdraw from their CPF Account.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It is unfortunate that there is a habit of rushing to publicise cases of persons in need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Instead, I would advise members of the public and Members of the Chamber to let social services know of such cases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I hope that we can agree that it is more important to first be assured that such individuals are, indeed, receiving the help they need, rather than to use them to prove or substantiate one’s policy or political arguments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: When cases are publicised with errors of fact, they create the misleading impression that we as a society are failing those of us who are in need.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Does the Senior Parliamentary Secretary agree that this response from the Government, in this case, will instil some fear in residents against sharing their worries with people who are genuinely trying to assist them and seeking to assist them?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think, in the whole process, we have been very mindful to make sure that the anonymity of the couple is assured.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In the Ministry of Social and Family Development's (MSF's) statement that was issued on 15 February as well as on the factual clarifications that were made on Factually.gov.sg, I think we had done our utmost to be assured of that.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think the whole exercise was to put out the facts and that is what it was all about.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked a question on the disclosure of private data.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: On the same note, I would like to ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary whether MSF knows how Mr Leong Mun Wai came to know about the couple and their personal difficulties?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I am just wondering whether there is any information leak from any agencies that had been dealing with the couple?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Perhaps the Senior Parliamentary Secretary could clarify that.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But this is what we know of Mr Leong Mun Wai's involvement.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Following the post by Mr Leong on 12 February, our volunteers spoke with the couple to find out what had happened because we know the couple and we had been helping them consistently, and that what Mr Leong had put out contained falsehoods.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The couple told our volunteers that they were surprised to find Mr Leong at the door on 12 February because they had neither approached the Progress Singapore Party (PSP) nor Mr Leong about their situation.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Instead, they said that they had actually written to Mr Pritam Singh four years ago in 2020.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Then, there was no response from the Workers' Party (WP) or Mr Pritam Singh.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Meanwhile, during these years, MSF and other Government agencies had been helping the couple and the extent of the help provided was set out in the MSF statement issued on 15 February.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The couple said that on 11 February, four years after they had written to Mr Singh, they received a call from him.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Singh spoke about the couple getting in touch with him four years ago and he told the couple that someone would visit them.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Then, one day later, on 12 February, Mr Leong Mun Wai went to visit the couple.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The couple told us that they were told that Mr Singh had informed Mr Leong regarding the email that Mr Singh had received four years ago.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As to why Mr Singh did not do anything for four years and why he then chose to speak with Mr Leong, and whether Mr Singh knew or agreed with Mr Leong that this matter will be highlighted on social media, just four days before the Budget Statement was due to be delivered on 16 February, that is not clear to us.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I do not know what Mr Singh was trying to do and I make no specific comment on his motivations.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But I am sure he and everyone in this Chamber here will agree with me that people, especially the vulnerable ones that we serve, and their plights should not be politicised.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Instead, there must be a sincere intent to help.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is an old art in politics – highlight one case, hopefully get attention, colour perceptions, then make people think negative thoughts about the Government as a whole.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Interesting that this happened a few days, just before the delivery of the Budget Statement on 16 February, perhaps to try to make people think that the Government does not help those who need help.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But whether that is anyone's motivation, I do not know and I cannot make a statement on that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, there was a letter sent by someone who had not left their address.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I picked up that letter as I was clearing up my files in my office.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I do not wish to reveal them here because I have not cleared these matters with that resident.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I was just checking in on them to say, "Look, are things better now?" That resident gave some feedback about still being in difficulty.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I asked for the address, since the address was not on the letter.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I realised that it was in an area where Mr Leong and his party are active.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, I said, "Look, have you seen your Social Service Office (SSO) or at least gone to the SSO?" The couple said, "No, we cannot, because I am blind." And the gentleman said that his wife was immobile.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For that reason, I got in touch with Mr Leong.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I said, "Look, if your team is visiting, you may want to find out and follow up." For the record, maybe the Senior Parliamentary Secretary knows this, I receive similar feedback from my own residents about trouble that some other people may be facing in a different constituency.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: He would have had knowledge of an email that I sent to the SSO — I beg your pardon, centrally to MSF, telling them, "Look, I have got this information.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can you please follow up with this resident who does not stay in any constituency which the WP are involved in?" So, I hope the MSF acknowledges that in this House, that this is how the WP operates as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: By the way, I did not know how Mr Leong Mun Wai followed up after that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But certainly, when we know of residents who are in trouble, who are in need, who are in difficulty, it is not in the WP's interest to go online and to point figures at Government agencies or point fingers at organisations like SSOs for no rhyme or reason.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Singh, we are approaching the end of Question Time and I want to allow the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to give a very short reply.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And so, the idea must always be: how do we follow up with this individual?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I hope that clarifies to MSF that when we know of residents who are in need in any constituency, we will try and get assistance rendered to them, be it through people who we know are active on the ground or through the MSF and SSO on their own.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Chua, if you can give a short reply, please.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think we set out to seek the facts.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And for us to add further stress to their situation by subjecting them to such situations, it is neither good faith nor does it do any good for their actual situations.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the Day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
